姚璹 is Yao Shu, not Yao Chong. 姚崇 is a different chief minister.
Yao Chong asked that a chief minister record deliberations on military and civil affairs in a "Current-Affairs Record" sent monthly to the Historiography Office.
Yao Shu asked that a chief minister record deliberations on military and civil affairs in a "Current-Affairs Record" sent monthly to the Historiography Office.
The subject is 姚璹, Yao Shu. Yao Chong names a different person.
Chong requested that one chief minister record the military and state affairs discussed, calling it the Current-Affairs Record, to be sent monthly to the History Office.
Shu requested that one chief minister record the military and state affairs discussed, calling it the Current-Affairs Record, to be sent monthly to the History Office.
璹 is Shu, not Chong. Chong would identify him with 姚崇.
In the eighth month of that year he suffered a sudden illness and died within a day and night, aged sixty-one.
In the eighth month of that year he suffered a sudden illness and died within two nights, aged sixty-one.
信宿 means a stay of two nights, not a single day and night.
Yuanliang rose to Director of the Left Bureau and died while serving as Attending Censor in charge of miscellaneous matters.
Yuanliang rose to Director of the Left Office and died while serving as Attending Censor in charge of miscellaneous matters.
左司郎中 is Director of the Left Office, the same title mistranslated as Left Bureau in Zhao Jing's grandfather's notice.
Yuanliang reached the post of Director of the Left Bureau and died while serving as Attending Censor with charge of miscellaneous matters.
Yuanliang reached the post of Director of the Left Office and died while serving as Attending Censor with charge of miscellaneous matters.
左司郎中 is Director of the Left Office, not of a Left Bureau.
Wei Lun was the son of Guangcheng, Military Governor of Shuofang under Xuanzong.
Wei Lun was the son of Guangcheng, Military Governor of Shuofang in the Kaiyuan and Tianbao eras.
The Chinese says 開元、天寶中 and does not name Xuanzong. The idiomatic sentence invents that sovereign.
In youth he received office by privilege as magistrate of Lantian.
In youth he received office by privilege as Warden of Lantian.
藍田縣尉 is the county warden or sheriff, not the magistrate. The literal already says Warden.
When An Lushan rebelled and the court fled to Shu, Lun was made Supervising Censor and marching sima on the Jiannan staff, then Vice Director of Revenue and Attending Censor.

When An Lushan rebelled and the court fled to Shu, Lun was made Investigating Censor and Campaign Marshal of the Jiannan command, concurrently acting judge for the Encampment Commissioner, then Vice Director of the Bureau of State Farms and concurrently Attending Censor.
屯田員外 is Vice Director of the Bureau of State Farms, not of Revenue, and 監察御史 is Investigating Censor. The idiomatic sentence also drops 置頓使判官.

When An Lushan rebelled and the imperial carriage went to Shu, Lun was appointed Supervising Censor and Marching Sima of the Jiannan Military Commission, concurrently Acting Judge of the Encampment Commissioner, and soon changed to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue and concurrently Attending Censor.

When An Lushan rebelled and the imperial carriage went to Shu, Lun was appointed Investigating Censor and Marching Sima of the Jiannan Military Commission, concurrently Acting Judge of the Encampment Commissioner, and soon changed to Vice Director of the Bureau of State Farms and concurrently Attending Censor.
屯田員外 belongs to the Bureau of State Farms, not the Ministry of Revenue, and 監察御史 is Investigating Censor.
In the end he suffered slander by inner eunuchs and was demoted to Registrar of Sima in Hengzhou.
In the end he suffered slander by inner eunuchs and was demoted to Household Administrator of Hengzhou.
衡州司戶 is the household office of Hengzhou. The literal adds Sima, which the Chinese does not have.
When Luoyang and Henan fell and transport routes were severed, Di Wuqi recommended Lun and appointed him Prefect of Shang, charged with collecting rent and tax on the Jing-Xiang routes.

When Luoyang and Henan fell and transport routes were severed, Di Wuqi recommended Lun for his ability to govern, and Lun was appointed Prefect of Shangzhou, charged with rent and tax on the Jing-Xiang circuits.
薦 is Di Wuqi's recommendation. 拜 is the appointment and is not said to be Di's own act. The idiomatic sentence fuses them.

When both the Eastern Capital and Henan fell to the rebels and the grain transport routes were cut, Revenue Commissioner Di Wuqi recommended Lun as a man of governing ability and appointed him Prefect of Shangzhou, charged as Rent and Tax Commissioner for Jing-Xiang and other circuits.

When both the Eastern Capital and Henan fell to the rebels and the grain transport routes were cut, Revenue Commissioner Di Wuqi recommended Lun as a man of governing ability, and Lun was appointed Prefect of Shangzhou, charged as Rent and Tax Commissioner for Jing-Xiang and other circuits.
The text separates Di Wuqi's recommendation from the appointment. The literal makes Di the one who appointed him.
Jiayan then seized Jiangling to the south, cutting grain routes on the Han and Mian; the court faced famine with growing alarm.
Jiayan then seized Jiangling to the south, cutting grain transport on the Han and Mian; the court ate late in anxiety.
旰食 means the court took its meals late from anxiety. It does not say the court faced famine.
荊、襄 are the two prefectures. Rendering 荊 as Jing collides with Zhao Jing, who is Jing throughout this chapter.
Jing and Xiang two prefectures were pacified.
The two prefectures of Jingzhou and Xiangzhou were pacified.
荊 is Jingzhou, not the person Zhao Jing. Xiang is Xiangzhou.
Before Lun could depart he was transferred to Prefect of Qin, concurrently Censor-in-Chief and Defense Commissioner.
Before Lun could depart he was transferred to Prefect of Qin, concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief and Defense Commissioner.
御史中丞 is Vice Censor-in-Chief, not Censor-in-Chief.
Lun had received the commission but had not yet departed when he was changed to Prefect of Qinzhou, concurrently Censor-in-Chief and Defense Commissioner of that prefecture.
Lun had received the commission but had not yet departed when he was changed to Prefect of Qinzhou, concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief and Defense Commissioner of that prefecture.
御史中丞 is Vice Censor-in-Chief.
His troops were few and without reinforcements; he frequently met defeat, was demoted in succession to Long Secretary of Bazhou and Warden of Wuchuan in Sizhou.
His troops were few and without reinforcements; he frequently met defeat and was demoted in succession to Administrator of Bazhou and Warden of Wuchuan County in Sizhou.
巴州長史 is Administrator of Bazhou, not Long Secretary, and 思州務川縣尉 is Warden of Wuchuan in Sizhou.
When eunuch Lü Taiyi forged an edict to raise troops in Lingnan, Lun was made Prefect of Shao, Censor-in-Chief, and commander of Shao, Lian, and Liu.
When eunuch Lü Taiyi forged an edict to raise troops in Lingnan, Lun was made Prefect of Shao, Vice Censor-in-Chief, and commander of Shao, Lian, and Liu.
御史中丞 is Vice Censor-in-Chief.

Because the inner eunuch Lü Taiyi in Lingnan forged an edict to recruit troops in rebellion, Lun was appointed Prefect of Shaozhou, concurrently Censor-in-Chief and Commander-in-Chief of Sha, Lian, and Liu.

Because the inner eunuch Lü Taiyi in Lingnan forged an edict to recruit troops in rebellion, Lun was appointed Prefect of Shaozhou, concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief and Commander-in-Chief of Shao, Lian, and Liu.
御史中丞 is Vice Censor-in-Chief.
In the end he suffered Taiyi's use of bribes and counterplots and was demoted in succession to Registrar of Sima in Xinzhou, Registrar in Qianzhou, Registrar in Suizhou, and Secretary in Suizhou.

In the end he suffered Taiyi's use of bribes and counterplots and was demoted in succession to Adjutant of Xinzhou, Household Administrator of Qianzhou, Household Administrator of Suizhou, and Adjutant of Suizhou.
信州司馬 is Adjutant of Xinzhou, not Registrar of Sima. 司戶 is household administrator. The Chinese names 隋州 and 隨州 separately.
Dezong sought men fit for distant missions and summoned Lun as Vice Director of Sacrifices and Censor-in-Chief, envoy to Tibet.
Dezong sought men fit for distant missions and summoned Lun as Vice Director of Sacrifices and Vice Censor-in-Chief, envoy to Tibet.
御史中丞 is Vice Censor-in-Chief.

When Dezong took the throne, he selected men fit to serve in distant regions and summoned Lun, appointing him Vice Director of the Court for Imperial Sacrifices and concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief, bearing credentials as envoy for harmony with Tibet.
御史中丞 is Vice Censor-in-Chief.
In Tibet he proclaimed imperial grace and the reach of Tang power; the Tibetans were pleased and the tsenpo sent tribute.
In Tibet he proclaimed imperial grace and the reach of the state's authority and virtue; the Tibetans were pleased and the tsenpo sent tribute.
國威德 is the state's authority and virtue. The idiomatic sentence invents the name Tang.
On his return he was promoted to Director of the Court for Imperial Sacrifices and concurrently Censor-in-Chief, with addition of Silver-Green Commissioner with the Splendid Purse.
On his return he was promoted to Director of the Court for Imperial Sacrifices and concurrently Censor-in-Chief, and was additionally granted Silver-Green Glorious Grand Master.
銀青光祿大夫 is the prestige title Silver-Green Glorious Grand Master, not a commissioner with a splendid purse.
Chief Minister Lu Qi disliked him and moved him to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, later adding Grand Master of the Palace.
Chief Minister Lu Qi disliked him and moved him to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, later adding the honor of Opening an Office with Ceremonies Equal to the Three Excellencies.
太子少保 is Junior Guardian, not Junior Tutor (少師). 開府儀同三司 is not merely Grand Master of the Palace.

He was again hated by Chief Minister Lu Qi and was changed to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, with cumulative addition of Grand Master of the Palace with the Splendid Purse bearing the Golden Seal.

He was again hated by Chief Minister Lu Qi and was changed to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, with cumulative addition of the honor of Opening an Office with Ceremonies Equal to the Three Excellencies.
The literal invents a splendid purse and golden seal. The Chinese has only 開府儀同三司, and 少保 is Junior Guardian.
During the Jingzhou mutiny the emperor fled to Fengtian.
During the mutiny of the Jingyuan troops the emperor fled to Fengtian.
涇師 is the Jingyuan army, not Jingzhou. Jingzhou would collide with other Jing names in this chapter.
When the Jingzhou troops rebelled, the imperial carriage went to Fengtian.
When the Jingyuan troops rebelled, the imperial carriage went to Fengtian.
涇師之亂 is the mutiny of the Jingyuan troops, not Jingzhou troops.

When Lu Qi, Bai Zhizhen, Zhao Zan, and others were demoted and Guan Bo was removed from chief minister to Minister of Justice, Lun wept in court: "The chief ministers failed to counsel the throne and brought the empire to this pass.
The idiomatic sentence drops 白誌貞 and 趙贊, whom the Chinese and the literal both name.
Yet he remains Minister of Revenue—how can the realm be governed?"
Yet he remains Minister of Justice—how can the realm be governed?
尚書 continues Guan Bo's 刑部尚書. It is not the Ministry of Revenue.
Yet he remains Minister of Revenue—how can the realm attain good order?"
Yet he remains Minister of Justice—how can the realm attain good order?
The preceding clause makes him Minister of Justice, not Minister of Revenue.

When Li Chulin held Vice Director of the Court for Imperial Sacrifices and Li Zhongcheng held Minister of Works and Vice Director of the Palace Domestic Service, Lun memorialized: "Chulin is violent and rebellious, and Zhongcheng is a vile barbarian—they do not belong in the pure ranks."

When Li Chulin held Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and concurrently Director of the Court of the Imperial Regalia, and Li Zhongcheng held a ministry and concurrently Director of the Palace Directorate, Lun memorialized: "Chulin is violent and rebellious, and Zhongcheng is a vile western barbarian—they do not belong in the pure ranks."
僕射兼衛尉卿 is Vice Director of State Affairs plus Director of the Imperial Regalia, not the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. 少府監 is Director of the Palace Directorate, and 尚書 is not specified as Works.

At that time Li Chulin held the post of Vice Director while also Director of the Court for Imperial Sacrifices, and Li Zhongcheng held the post of Minister while also Vice Director of the Palace Domestic Service; Lun submitted a memorial saying: "Chulin is violent and rebellious, Zhongcheng a vile sort from the western barbarians—they should not stand in the pure ranks."

At that time Li Chulin held Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and concurrently Director of the Court of the Imperial Regalia, and Li Zhongcheng held a ministry and concurrently Director of the Palace Directorate; Lun submitted a memorial saying: "Chulin is violent and rebellious, Zhongcheng a vile sort from the western barbarians—they should not stand in the pure ranks."
衛尉卿 is the Court of the Imperial Regalia, not Imperial Sacrifices, and 少府監 is its director, not a vice director.
He passed both classics examinations and was appointed magistrate of Linqing in Bei Prefecture.
He passed both classics examinations and was appointed warden of Linqing in Bei Prefecture.
臨清縣尉 is the county warden, not the magistrate. The literal already says Warden.
He memorialized on current affairs and was made magistrate of Zhengping in Jiang.
He memorialized on current affairs and was made warden of Zhengping in Jiang.
正平尉 is a county warden, not a magistrate.

On the Hedong staff he became Acting Vice Director of the Bureau of Catering, Vice Governor of Taiyuan, and Deputy Regent of the Northern Capital.
膳部員外郎 is a bureau vice director, not Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites, and 北都副留守 is Deputy Regent of the Northern Capital, not a military governor.
He served on the staff in Hedong, was appointed Acting Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites, Junior Vice Director of Taiyuan, and Deputy Military Governor of the Northern Capital.
He served on the staff in Hedong and was appointed Acting Vice Director of the Bureau of Catering, Vice Governor of Taiyuan, and Deputy Regent of the Northern Capital.
膳部員外郎 is not Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites, and 副留守 is not Deputy Military Governor.
He later served as Acting Director of Rites and deputy commissioner, then Prefect of Fen.
He later served as Acting Director of the Bureau of Rites and deputy military commissioner, then Prefect of Fen.
禮部郎中 is Director of the Bureau of Rites, not of the whole ministry.
He was again Acting Director of the Ministry of Rites and Deputy Military Commissioner, and was changed to Prefect of Fenzhou.
He was again Acting Director of the Bureau of Rites and Deputy Military Commissioner, and was changed to Prefect of Fenzhou.
禮部郎中 is a bureau director. Director of the Ministry of Rites would be a different and higher post.

In the second month of the first year of Xingyuan, Dan's Marching Sima Fan Ze reported affairs at the mobile court; after Ze had reported back and a great feast for the generals was underway, an urgent dispatch arrived saying Ze had replaced Dan as military governor and Dan was summoned as Minister of Works.
The literal says 'a urgent,' which is ungrammatical, and it misses that the feast was already underway when the dispatch arrived. 方大宴諸將 means Dan was then feasting the generals.
Soon he became Military Governor of the Eastern Capital and Defense Commissioner of the eastern metropolitan region.
Soon, in his regular office, he became Regent of the Eastern Capital and Defense Commissioner of the eastern metropolitan district and Runan.
東都留守 is Regent of the Eastern Capital, not its military governor, and 汝南 is Runan, which the idiomatic sentence drops.
Soon with his regular office he became Military Governor of the Eastern Capital and Defense Commissioner of the Eastern Metropolitan Region and Runan.
Soon, with his regular office, he became Regent of the Eastern Capital and Defense Commissioner of the Eastern Metropolitan District and Runan.
留守 is regent, not military governor.
Thousands of Li Na's men marching home asked to camp outside Hua.
Several thousand of Li Na's soldiers were returning to their camps and passed Huazhou; the senior general asked to lodge them outside the city.
大將請 means the senior general asked to quarter them outside, not that the soldiers themselves asked.
The 'Nine Mounds' is the ancient classic on which Cheng Fu was based; the six forms are the new idea in maps.
The Nine Mounds is the ancient classic of the territorial accounts; the six forms are the new idea of mapping.
成賦之古經 is the ancient classic concerned with territorial descriptions. It is not a work titled Cheng Fu.

In the seventeenth year he finished the Map of Chinese and Barbarians Within the Seas and a forty-scroll geographical account, and submitted them, saying:
至十七年 continues the Zhenyuan year count. It is not Jia Dan's seventeenth year of age.
Wuqiu marched east and inscribed his victory;
Guanqiu marched east and inscribed a victory at Bunai.
毋丘 is the compound surname Guanqiu, not Wuqiu, and 不耐 is the place inscribed.
In former times Wuqiu went out with the army and eastward inscribed Bu Nai.
In former times Guanqiu went out with the army and eastward inscribed Bunai.
毋丘 is read Guanqiu. The literal Wuqiu splits the surname as if it were a personal name Wu Qiu.

Xuanzong by great filial piety cleared the inner realm and by non-action governed the outer; Dayuan horses were recorded yearly and filled the inner stables. Compared with the Ershi general's exhausted troops and reckless war, how could they be put in the same class!
豈同年哉 means they cannot be classed together. It does not mean the same calendar year. 大宛 is Dayuan, and 貳師 is the Ershi general.
In the tenth month of Jianzhong 4 (783) the Jingzhou mutiny broke out.
In the tenth month of Jianzhong 4 (783) the Jingyuan troops seized the palace.
涇師 is the Jingyuan army, not Jingzhou, and 犯闕 means they attacked the palace. The same mistranslation of Jingzhou for the Jingyuan mutiny occurs earlier in this chapter.
In the tenth month of the fourth year of Jianzhong the Jingzhou troops violated the palace.
In the tenth month of the fourth year of Jianzhong the Jingyuan troops violated the palace.
涇師犯闕 is the Jingyuan troops violating the palace, not Jingzhou troops.

Zhi privately told him: "I once saw Chancellor Dou at Chenzhou, who said he had recommended you several times, but the emperor's will did not allow it and there were angry words about you."
竇相 is Chancellor Dou, the Dou Can named two sentences later, not a man named Dou Xiang. 郴州 is Chenzhou. 予 is Lu Zhi speaking, and 為公 is 'for you.'

Jiang was rash and Zhao dangerous; both leaped the heavenly road.

Jiang was rash, Zhao dangerous—both leaped the heavenly road.

The encomium says: Yuanjing's grand plans—truly he may be called a pure Confucian.
真謂純儒 means he may truly be called a pure Confucian. 'Marked a true Confucian' weakens 純 and turns the judgment into a description of the counsel alone.
